kept.title: Remote Code Execution via arbitrary worker task file
kept.description: The `getHandler` function in `src/entry/utils.ts` uses dynamic `import(filename)` based on user-supplied parameters to load and execute code within the worker process.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker identifies an application using tinypool that accepts user input for the 'filename' parameter in `run()`.
Attacker points the filename to a local file containing malicious JS code (e.g., /tmp/malicious.mjs).
Tinypool executes the imported module as a worker task.
Arbitrary code runs in the worker process context.
kept.impact: Full code execution within the worker process, leading to potential sandbox escape or data exfiltration.

kept.title: Unsafe ESLint rules suppressing security checks
kept.description: ESLint configuration disables critical safety rules such as `no-unsafe-assignment` and `no-explicit-any`, which hides potential type-confusion and injection vulnerabilities across the codebase.
steps_to_exploit: An attacker identifies a codebase contributor using the disabled rules to bypass type safety.
An unsafe assignment or type-mismatch is introduced that allows arbitrary data to reach sensitive execution points.
The vulnerability remains undetected by automated CI linting.
kept.impact: Increased probability of introducing exploitable vulnerabilities that static analysis tools would otherwise catch.

kept.title: Insecure Process Forking via unsanitized environment variables
kept.description: `ProcessWorker` initializes child processes using user-supplied env options without strict validation, potentially allowing environment injection.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker controls the options passed to the `Tinypool` constructor.
Attacker injects malicious shell variables or configuration flags into the `env` object.
The child process inherits these variables, leading to altered behavior or privilege escalation.
kept.impact: Compromised execution environment of the child process.

kept.title: Improper Serialization of Error Objects
kept.description: The `serializeError` function spreads all enumerable properties of an Error object. This can lead to sensitive internal state leakage to the main thread.
steps_to_exploit: Trigger an error within a worker that contains sensitive data attached as a property to the Error object.
The main thread receives the serialized error and exposes the sensitive data to the calling code or logs.
Sensitive information is leaked outside the worker's security boundary.
kept.impact: Exposure of internal worker state or sensitive runtime data.

kept.title: Potential Prototype Pollution via Object.assign/spread
kept.description: Several areas of the code use spread operators and manual object manipulation on user-supplied options without filtering dangerous properties like `__proto__`.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker provides a malicious options object with a `__proto__` property.
The object is spread or merged into `kDefaultOptions` or other configurations.
Prototype pollution occurs, affecting all objects of that type across the application.
kept.impact: Global application state manipulation leading to denial of service or code execution.

kept.title: Exposure of Internals via `process.__tinypool_state__`
kept.description: The library attaches an object to the global `process` variable which is accessible to any script running within the same process.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker injects a malicious script into the runtime environment (e.g., via dependency confusion or secondary vulnerability).
Attacker reads `process.__tinypool_state__` to gain insights into worker IDs and internal data.
Attacker uses this information to craft targeted exploits against internal messaging channels.
kept.impact: Exposure of internal metadata to other modules within the same process.

kept.title: Lack of Input Validation for Task Metadata
kept.description: The `name` parameter in `runTask` is used as an object property key to resolve handlers, but is never validated to prevent prototype lookups.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker calls `run(..., { name: 'toString' })`.
The lookup logic attempts to access a handler that may be a built-in method or sensitive function.
Unexpected code execution or crashes occur when `handler(task)` is called.
kept.impact: Unexpected behavior or denial of service through improper property access.

kept.title: Insecure `new Function` usage for ESM import
kept.description: The use of `new Function` to bypass transpilation is an anti-pattern that mimics `eval`, potentially bypassing security filters.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker identifies a context where this function is called with attacker-controlled input.
Though currently used for a static string, any future modification could allow arbitrary code execution via the dynamic string constructor.

kept.title: Resource Exhaustion via unrestricted worker creation
kept.description: The pool allows spawning threads up to `maxThreads`. Without strict limits on the number of pools or total global threads, a process can be exhausted of system resources.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker causes the application to instantiate multiple `Tinypool` instances.
Each instance spawns up to `maxThreads` processes.
System memory and CPU are exhausted, leading to a crash.

kept.title: Unsafe Message Handling on child process channel
kept.description: Messages received on the parent-worker channel are parsed and processed without checking the sender's origin or message integrity.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker compromises the child process.
Attacker sends a spoofed message that the parent treats as a valid response for a specific `taskId`.
The main process continues execution using corrupted data returned by the attacker.

kept.title: Potential Memory Leak in `handlerCache`
kept.description: The cache mechanism in `getHandler` has a limit of 1000 items, but an attacker can rapidly populate this cache with junk keys to force evictions and trigger high memory/GC churn.
steps_to_exploit: Repeatedly call `run()` with distinct, high-entropy filenames or names.
Force the system to constantly reload modules and evict cache entries.
Application performance degrades due to constant I/O and memory pressure.

kept.title: Insecure Path Handling in `maybeFileURLToPath`
kept.description: The logic to convert file URLs to paths is simplistic and susceptible to path traversal if input is not carefully sanitized.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker provides a URL like 'file://../../etc/passwd'.
The utility may resolve this to an arbitrary location on the disk, potentially allowing access to sensitive files during `import()`.

kept.title: Hardcoded SIGKILL Timeout
kept.description: The `SIGKILL_TIMEOUT` of 1000ms is fixed, which might not be sufficient for workers to perform orderly cleanup, causing inconsistent state.
steps_to_exploit: Attacker performs a resource-intensive task that takes >1s to finalize.
Worker is SIGKILLed before the database or file handles can be closed, leading to corruption or dangling resources.

kept.title: Excessive Listener Limits on Stdin/out
kept.description: The pool increases max listener counts on standard streams for every worker created, which can lead to memory exhaustion.
steps_to_exploit: Create thousands of workers.
The process's memory footprint explodes due to the accumulation of event listener arrays on the standard streams.
Application crashes due to OOM.

kept.title: Dependabot configured for daily updates
kept.description: The dependabot configuration is present but may not be sufficient for immediate mitigation of zero-day vulnerabilities in critical dependencies.
steps_to_exploit: A zero-day is found in a dependency (e.g., `vitest`).
Attacker exploits the vulnerability before the daily scan runs or before the PR is merged.
The system remains vulnerable for an extended window.
